Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually come with too many software limitations. The platform can run most major computer applications, and there's a large selection of Mac-exclusive, practical applications available.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, recent testing shows that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games currently perform on Mac better than ever before...

Apple has its own dedicated game porting toolkit that helps developers evaluate how their Windows games will run on Mac, with the goal of encouraging and facilitating game ports to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito points out, this toolkit is also being used by players to unofficially run Windows software on Mac — and he is one of them. He notes that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, citing GTA V as an example.

After testing the fourth beta version of the game porting toolkit for several days on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro chip, he found that these performance improvements essentially transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games... On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using identical in-game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from approximately 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to approximately 176 fps in the GPTK 4 beta, an improvement of roughly 66%. The game runs quite smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledges that not every game will see such dramatic improvements, but he hopes these advances will encourage game developers to consider Mac as a viable platform.
